title: The Proton — Discovery & Properties of Anode Rays
topicTitle: Orbitals and shape of s and p orbitals only
notes: **Proton definition:** a proton is a positively charged subatomic particle denoted with the symbol p⁺.

**Context of discovery:** it was discovered after the discovery of electrons, with the assumption that positive particles must also exist alongside negative particles since an atom is electrically neutral.
**Discovery (1886):** the proton was discovered by Eugen Goldstein by a discharge tube experiment like that for electrons.
**Experiment:** he passed high voltage electricity through a discharge tube filled with hydrogen gas and provided with a perforated metal cathode.
**Low pressure:** the discharge was carried out at low pressure.
**Canal rays:** he observed rays travelling opposite to the cathode rays; these were deflected towards the cathode of the applied field and thus called anode rays, positive rays, or canal rays.

**Properties of anode rays:** (a) they cast a shadow of the objects in their path; (b) they travel in a straight line; (c) they are deflected towards the cathode of the applied electric or magnetic field; (d) they cause a heating effect on metal coils; (e) they rotate a small paddle wheel placed on their path.
**Conclusion:** these properties led to the conclusion that anode rays carry a positive charge and possess a certain mass.
**Naming:** these rays were named protons by Goldstein and symbolized with p⁺.
**Charge:** the proton possesses +1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ coulomb of electric charge, equal but opposite in sign to that of an electron.
**Mass:** a proton is much heavier than an electron; its mass is 1.672 × 10⁻²⁴ g, equal to the mass of the hydrogen atom.
